findings.description: Applying D1 and FR-4 changes observable behaviour for one input. At baseline a callback with a null payment_id gets the normal ok response, because the NOT NULL IntegrityError is swallowed as a duplicate and fulfil() still runs. After the change it raises out of CallbackController.handle. The plan argues that FR-4 and D1 require this and that the sources define the unchanged contract only for first deliveries and duplicates, which is a defensible reading (OQ-1 is open and non-blocking). It is nonetheless a change to existing provider-facing behaviour that AC-2 and NFR-1 protect. The plan flags it for the approver in A9 and Risks, so no plan change is required, but the human gate should confirm it explicitly.
evidence: app/payment_service/callback_controller.py:19-24 (no input validation, response independent of fulfilled)
findings.plan_section: A9; Risks 'Behaviour change for a malformed callback'; AC-2
findings.required_action: None for the Plan Author. The approver should confirm at the human gate that the null-payment_id behaviour change is acceptable under AC-2, as A9 already states.

findings.description: T6 releases N threads at the same time, each constructing its own PaymentRepository, so the first-ever CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS on an empty database also races. A failure there would be an OperationalError from setup, not evidence about the idempotency logic, and the plan would have to sort out which one it was. The plan does intend T6 to probe DDL contention and treats any change as a flagged deviation, so this is only a note for the implementer. A per-thread repository constructed inside its own thread is also required because sqlite3 connections use check_same_thread=True by default, and the plan's factory design already satisfies this.
findings.plan_section: T6; Risks 'Lock contention from per-request CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS'
findings.required_action: Optional: have T6 pre-create the table once (for example by constructing and closing one repository) before the barrier, and run a separate empty-database race case, so a DDL failure is distinguishable from an idempotency failure.

prior_findings.note: Checked against app/payment_service/repository.py:22-24 and :39-40, where the baseline maps every IntegrityError to False and payment_id is NOT NULL. The plan now makes T1 change record_if_new so that it returns False only when the error message contains 'UNIQUE constraint failed: processed_callbacks.provider_event_id'. Any other IntegrityError is rolled back and re-raised. There is no SELECT-before-INSERT and no lock, which keeps the constraint the sole arbiter and matches guidance D1 and the Python 3.10 constraint. T4(c) and T4(d) test the NULL payment_id case at repository level, including that the connection is left clean. T5(c) tests it at service level, checking that fulfilment is not called, release is not called and no 'duplicate' log is emitted. The FR-4 traceability row is corrected and no longer says only non-IntegrityError failures are non-duplicates. PLAN-002 and PLAN-003 (advisory) are also addressed by A10 with an operational check, by T0 baseline capture, by controller-level equality in T6 and by a case-insensitive grep guard.

review.summary: The revised plan resolves the previous blocking finding. record_if_new is narrowed so that only a provider_event_id PRIMARY KEY violation returns False and any other sqlite3.IntegrityError is re-raised. The plan cites and applies developer guidance D1, G-C1 and G-C2 correctly, and the guidance does not conflict with the Planning Context or governance. The normalized context matches the three raw sources, with no invented or weakened criteria, and the design satisfies C-1 to C-8 and FR-1 to FR-8, including C-3 (delete-then-reinsert under the same constraint, no status compare-and-swap) and C-4 (per-request repository via a factory). The repository claims were checked against the source and hold: the baseline discards record_if_new's result, there is one construction site, in test_payment_service.py, and the controller ignores ProcessingResult.fulfilled. Only advisory observations remain, both already surfaced by the plan for the approver.
